newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, March 19.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.

- Irish government and opposition leaders on Tuesday called for a fresh inquiry into the events of Bloody Sunday following revelations about the actions of British soldiers who killed 14 demonstrators in Derry.
- A new Irish Broadcasting Commission to oversee the entire broadcasting sector is one of the main elements of government proposals formally unveiled on Tuesday.
- Computer giant IBM is to pay 400 employees in Ireland a 1996 bonus worth an average of 2,505 Irish pounds as part of its $1.2 billion worldwide bonus for its 241,000 employees.
- Irish beef exports face a serious new challenge to their share of the Russian beef market following the lifting by Russia of a ban on beef from Argentina.

- Ireland's Police Commissioner and the main organisation representing rank and file Irish police have disagreed over the significance of a court ruling that Irish police must identify informers to senior officers.
-Continuing speculation about a delay to the start of EU monetary union has led to a sharp fall in bond prices on the Dublin market and an increase in long-term interest rates.

- At least one-third of all women have been subjected to sexual harassment at work while the figure for men is just four percent according to research carried out on behalf of the European Commission.
- Ireland's Agriculture Minister Ivan Yates is poised to announce a 100 million Irish pounds windfall for farmers hit by losses arising out of the appreciation of the punt and the BSE crisis.

- Demands for a fresh inquiry into the events of Bloody Sunday gathered speed on Tuesday after Ireland's Prime Minister John Bruton declared that it would not be possible for the British to "comprehensively" reject new evidence from a Parachute Regiment soldier.
